title: ALMA Submillimeter Continuum Imaging of the Host Galaxies of GRB 021004 and GRB 080607
question: Do the GRB 021004 and GRB 080607 host galaxies at z>2 have significant dust-obscured star formation, and is the large afterglow extinction of the dark burst GRB 080607 representative of its host?

what.value: Infrared SED template library (105 templates) used to derive L_IR

evidence.quote: this can be done using the infrared spectral energy distribution (SED) library of (cite: chary01).

what.value: Stellar masses of hosts and optical photometry/SFRs for comparison

evidence.quote: The host galaxy of GRB 080607 has a better constrained stellar mass of 1–3 $\times10^{10} M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ (cite: chen11a).

external_data.citation: Chen et al. 2011a; Savaglio et al. 2009; Chen et al. 2009

recipe.method: Inspect JAO calibration, Fourier transform visibilities with natural weighting; dirty image for GRB 021004, CLEAN for GRB 080607
Point-source flux at host location; for GRB 080607 point-source and 2-D Gaussian fits
Redshift CE01 templates and select those consistent with the observed 345 GHz flux or upper limit; convert L_IR to SFR
assumptions: Dust temperature from CE01 luminosity-dependent templates; cosmology H0=71, OmegaM=0.27, OmegaL=0.73

evidence.quote: The 345 GHz point-source flux measured at the location of the host galaxy is $0.17\pm0.11$ mJy.

answer_key.quantity: L_IR upper limit GRB 021004 host (3 sigma)

evidence.quote: The inferred SFR is between 41 and 77 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$.
the 3-$\sigma$ upper limit of the SFR of the host galaxy is 53 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
we adopt the more conservative measurement of 0.31 mJy with a statistical significance of 3.3 $\sigma$.

not_stated_but_needed: Imaging parameters: cell size, image size, CLEAN threshold/mask, iterations

rediscovery_reason: Cycle 0 data are likely public, the recipe is short, and results are numeric fluxes.
